methodology: Waves and figures come from data/figures.json — 5 waves carry a 2026 year, plus the Store & Convention Exclusives bucket's 2026 entries. Release dates, windows, and announced MSRPs come from data/preorders.json (21 tracked items); announced prices are never market prices.

The Top 10 is scored, not vibes: each entry's documented distinctions are counted (first-ever figure = 2 points; first-since-a-year, notable pack-in, format distinction, archive-first, or documented 2026 market story = 1 each). Ties break alphabetically. Every distinction cites its record.

narrative.body: Hasbro has 'largely abandoned' short-packed chase figures in modern Marvel Legends, and no 2025–2026-era 6-inch chase was documented by the hobby press this year. The chase era — Toy Biz's finite redistributions, the art-deco variants produced 'with scarcity in mind' — is now history, and the Rarity Guide treats it as such. What replaced it isn't a new scarcity mechanic: it's the order window. The year's defining limited release, the Bastion & Bolivar Trask 2-pack, is made-to-order — scarcity measured in calendar days, not case ratios.
narrative.heading: The year the chase died

sources.label: Market briefing — the chase era ends

narrative.body: 2026 brought no packaging overhaul. Instead it brought the retro blister card back as the default canvas — the X-Men '97 wave, the Spider-Man: The Animated Series wave, and the Retro Venom reissue all ride retro cardbacks — and the mini comic as the pack-in of the year, with Mini Comics Wave 3 putting a physical comic in every box. After the plastic-free reversal of April 2023, the line's packaging story is settled: nostalgia on the front, sustainability in the materials.
narrative.heading: Retro is the packaging story

narrative.body: 2026 was the year the reissue program stopped being a rumor and became the market's central mechanism. The Pulse VHS-exclusive Animated Series figures sold out, escalated on the aftermarket — and came back on retro blister cards at the $27.99 standard. The 2021 Pulse Con cel-shaded Venom is back at Fan Channel for $34.99. NYCC added an Astonishing X-Men two-pack reissue. The pattern is now textbook: sellout → aftermarket spike → reissue → premium collapse. The open question is whether it keeps working at scale — the Fall 2026 waves' aftermarket behavior will be the first real test.
narrative.heading: The reissue machine

narrative.body: Reported-price coverage for 2026 is thin — seven figures, none of them 2026 releases — but it tells a coherent story. The white-deco Epic Heroes Doctor Doom is the modern chase-adjacent standout: $115–$200 in reported solds, closing at $200 on August 10, 2026, against roughly $60 in October 2024. The standard green Doom averaged $62.44 across 48 tracked sales. The $7,500 asking price on the unproduced Toy Biz Series 15 blue-and-white Wasp chase prototype (~10 carded) is an ask, not a sale — a two-decade-old artifact, not a 2026 discovery. And one retailer's October snapshot said it plainly: the older Colossus-BAF Cyclops sat in stock at $14.99 while the X-Men '97 Cyclops sold out. Demand concentrates where the cameras are.
narrative.heading: The aftermarket in miniature

narrative.body: The year isn't over. Doomsday Wave 2 pre-orders opened October 14, the X-Men '97 wave October 21, the Astonishing two-pack October 28; the YFNS Spider-Man vs. Rhino 2-pack hits Pulse November 1; the Bastion & Trask order window closes November 20; the TAS wave and Retro Venom ship in December. Every one of those is a live data point this retrospective will need when the year closes — check the release calendar and the pre-order tracker for the current state.
